name: Serbian Empire
alt: Empire of the Serbs and Romans

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Serbia (Nemanjić state)
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Serbia shape, the Nemanjić kingdom before the imperial title

predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Byzantine Macedonia (to Kavala, Serres taken 25 September 1345), Epirus, Aetolia and Acarnania (1347) and Thessaly (1348)

successors.name: Moravian Serbia
successors.text: Lazar Hrebeljanović's principality in the Morava valley (Cliopatria's Serbian Empire shape from 1375)

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Macedonia, where after Maritsa 'Ottoman troops advanced' and regional lords such as Prince Marko became Ottoman vassals

successors.name: Albanian principalities
successors.text: Albania, which by 1371 had 'entirely seceded from Serbia'

successors.name: Despotate of Arta
successors.text: Epirus, Thessaly and Albania 'had entirely seceded from Serbia' (Battle of Maritsa page); Cliopatria's Despotate of Arta row starts in 1375

successors.name: Zeta (Balšić lordship)
successors.text: Zeta, Kosovo and the lords of the west (Cliopatria's Serbian Despots row from 1375)

rulers.name: Stefan Dušan
rulers.title: Emperor and autocrat of Serbs and Romans

ledger.x: 1346: Valona becomes a Serbian vassal principality.
16 April 1346: Dušan is crowned Emperor at Skopje.
1347: Dušan takes Epirus, Aetolia and Acarnania.
1348: the Catalan part of Thessaly goes to the Serbs.
Spring 1356: Orsini takes Thessaly from the Serbs.
1356: Simeon Uroš breaks away at Kostur (Kastoria).
ledger.cp: Simeon Uroš (Emperor of Serbs and Greeks)

ledger.x: By 1371: the Battle of Maritsa page has 'Thessaly, Albania and Epirus had entirely seceded from Serbia' by 1371; no page opened dates the secession (the Balšić page: the brothers were 'oblastni gospodari of Zeta' in edicts of Uroš (r.
26 September 1371: the Ottomans beat the Serbs at Maritsa.

December 1371: the empire ends and the Macedonian lords fall into the Ottoman orbit (the page says regional lords like Prince Marko 'became Ottoman vassals'); the end of the contest at the dissolution is the researcher's bridge, since the page does not say when the Ottoman advance stopped.
4 December 1371: Uroš V dies childless and the empire ends.

wars.name: Serbian conquest of Byzantine lands
wars.outcome: Serbian victory: Serres (25 September 1345), the Athonite monks (November 1345), Epirus, Aetolia and Acarnania (1347) and Thessaly (1348); Dušan took no Peloponnese and no Thessaloniki.

wars.name: Dušan's war in Bosnia and Hum
wars.outcome: Dušan 'invaded Hum' in October 1350 with an army 'said to be of 80,000'; Ban Stephen II Kotromanić avoided battle and the page records no final result.

wars.name: Hungarian invasion of Serbia
wars.outcome: The Hungarians 'managed to occupy part of northern Serbia' in 1354; peace with Louis I in May 1355.

wars.name: Orsini's invasion of Thessaly
wars.outcome: Orsini overran Thessaly in spring 1356 and drove Simeon Uroš from Aetolia and Acarnania; Simeon retook Epirus and Thessaly in 1359 under his own 'emperor of Serbs and Greeks' title.

wars.name: Battle of Maritsa
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory on 26 September 1371; Vukašin and Uglješa Mrnjavčević killed; Ottoman troops advanced into Macedonia and Prince Marko and other lords became Ottoman vassals; Uroš V died in December and the empire ended.

certainty.note: No treaty line survives in the pages opened for the empire's frontiers; the 1334 peace with Byzantium (Ohrid, Prilep, Strumica) pre-dates it, and the Danube-Sava northern border is the one firm line (Stefan Lazarević page for the later…
